subject: Exit-channel operator playbook + IP binding / handoff for Redwood Private
messages:
From: ops@aurorahealth.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: peter.tan@netsec-consulting.com
Date: 2027-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: exit-channel operator playbook + IP binding details for private deployment

Hi Marissa / David,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aurora's infra team wants to lock down the Private deployment egress surface before we proceed to the staging rollout. We have a few concrete asks:

- A short "operator playbook" we can hand to our network/security ops team explaining how Redwood Private uses outbound connections (control plane, model pull, telemetry).
- A definitive list of IPs / FQDNs that must be allowlisted on our perimeter firewall, and any notes about ephemeral ranges or NAT behavior.
- Any required port/protocol details (health checks, api/metrics endpoints, TLS/SNI expectations, mutual TLS if applicable).
- A verification checklist we can use during acceptance (smoke tests, curl/openssl checks, log evidence to gather).

Can you send a draft operator playbook and an initial mapping of IPs this week? We're aiming for a staging cutover on Dec 8.

Also cc'ing Peter from the external netsec engagement — he will validate the firewall rules on our side.

Thanks,
Maya Lopez
Aurora Health — Platform Ops

Date: 2027-11-25T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: exit-channel operator playbook + IP binding details for private deployment

Maya / Peter,

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached an initial operator playbook draft (operator-playbook-draft.pdf) and asked David to enumerate the exact egress IPs and the acceptance checklist. High-level notes below so your SREs have context before the doc review:

- Redwood Private has two logical outbound categories: (1) Control plane telemetry / agent callbacks (to the Redwood control plane) and (2) Model fetch & runtime traffic (during scale/updates).
- Our control plane endpoints are reachable over standard HTTPS (443) and use SNI matching. For most customers we recommend allowlisting DNS names + the short set of static egress CIDRs we provide.
- We do support client certificate-based mTLS for sensitive installs — mention if Aurora requires this and we'll enable the cert exchange flow.

Next steps: David will send the IP mapping + firewall snippets. After that we can sync on a 30-minute runbook walkthrough (I propose Tue 11/30 10:00 PT). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include Karthik for on-call handoff details.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[attachment: operator-playbook-draft.pdf]

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: ops@aurorahealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, peter.tan@netsec-consulting.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-27T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: exit-channel operator playbook + IP binding details for private deployment

Hi Maya / Peter,

Below is a concrete set of requirements and a verification checklist. This is intended for your perimeter firewall and proxy team. The attached spreadsheet (egress-ip-mapping.xlsx) maps each function to an IP block and a suggested FQDN.

1) Egress categories and recommended rules

  A) Control plane callbacks (mandatory for management/rollouts):
    - Purpose: telemetry, rollout state, license heartbeat, remote config.
    - IPs (example static CIDRs we will provide in the final package): 34.210.120.0/24, 52.23.14.128/26
    - DNS / FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com (we recommend allowlisting both FQDN and CIDR where possible).
    - Ports: TCP 443 (HTTPS).
    - TLS: SNI present; server certs validated by public CA. Optional client certs (mTLS) available on request for enterprise installs.

  B) Model artifact fetch + runtime coordination (can be heavy during model pulls):
    - Purpose: retrieving model shards, embeddings indices, checksum verification.
    - IPs: 3.140.55.0/24 (artifact CDN), 18.197.22.0/25 (secondary mirror).
    - Ports: TCP 443.
    - Notes: These addresses are generally static for a given region but may include ephemeral URLs for scale. We provide an "artifact manifest" RSS that lists mirrors used during a given rollout.

  C) Optional telemetry / metrics ingestion endpoints (customer may proxy):
    - If you require all telemetry to route via your egress proxy, we can configure the agent to forward via a customer-provided proxy (HTTP/HTTPS). Must support large POST bodies (up to 4 MB) and keep-alive.

2) Firewall & NAT considerations

  - Source NATing: If you have outbound NAT in your VPC, we need a stable egress IP range or a predictable NAT pool; ephemeral NAT makes IP-based allowlisting fragile. If you cannot provide static NAT, use DNS + port restrictions and provide signed SNI/ClientCert verification.
  - Ephemeral IPs / rotation: We support documentation of planned rotation windows. During rotation, there will be a small window (~30s) where rollouts may briefly fallback — plan a canary to avoid user impact.
  - DNS caching: Agents will cache control.redwood-inference.com for TTL=60s. If your perimeter rewrites DNS or uses split-horizon, ensure that the returned A records map to the allowed CIDRs.

3) Minimal firewall rule examples (egress rules on your perimeter):

  - Allow TCP 443 to 34.210.120.0/24 (control plane) with SNI control.redwood-inference.com
  - Allow TCP 443 to 3.140.55.0/24 (artifact CDN) with SNI artifacts.redwood-inference.com
  - Allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver only (prevent direct external DNS to reduce cache poisoning).
  - Allow outbound NTP (UDP 123) to your time service; if blocked, TLS cert validation may fail.

4) Acceptance / verification checklist (run these during cutover):

  - From a host in your private runtime network: curl -v --resolve control.redwood-inference.com:443:34.210.120.12 "https://control.redwood-inference.com/healthz" should return 200 and include "redwood-control: ok" in the body.
  - TLS verification: openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername control.redwood-inference.com | grep "Verify return code: 0"
  - Artifact fetch: wget --header="Accept: application/json" https://artifacts.redwood-inference.com/manifest/2027-11-27-aurora.json should download the manifest and match the checksum in artifacts list.
  - Log evidence: Confirm your perimeter logs show outbound flows to the control-plane CIDR during the test window; export a 15-min capture and ship as gzipped JSON to our secure intake (we will provide a pre-signed S3 URL).

5) Operator handoff & on-call ownership (operational playbook items)

  - Handoff packet (what we will deliver): operator-playbook-draft.pdf, egress-ip-mapping.xlsx, ip-rotation-notice.txt, verification-scripts.sh.
  - On-call: Redwood SRE on-call (primary: karthik_iyer@redwood.com) will be available for the first 72 hours post-cutover for troubleshooting.
  - Escalation matrix: Standard Redwood escalation (SRE -> NetEng -> Director) included in the playbook; we'll attach a one-page laminated checklist for your ops team.

6) Additional hardening options (if Aurora needs strict allowlist-only posture)

  - mTLS client certs: we can issue customer-scoped client certs and public-key pin the session. Requires cert distribution and periodic rotation (we recommend 90 days).
  - SNI + cert pinning: require SNI match and verify server cert fingerprint in your proxy if you cannot base on IPs alone.
  - Proxy chaining: Redwood agent can route over your outbound proxy and attach X-Redwood-Agent metadata headers for attribution.

Acceptance criteria summary (for signoff):
  - All firewall rules above in place and tested via the verification checklist.
  - Evidence capture uploaded to Redwood intake (pre-signed S3) with perimeter logs and curl traces.
  - On-call contact confirmed and test call completed with your SRE.

If you want, we can produce a signed PDF of the IP list that your procurement/security team can keep. Let me know whether you need mTLS and whether your environment requires all outbound to flow via a customer proxy.

-David
David Kim
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: egress-ip-mapping.xlsx]

Maya —

Thanks for the thorough inputs. We reviewed David's mapping and Marissa's draft playbook. A few quick operational items to confirm before Tuesday's walkthrough:

- Karthik (cc) will be the Redwood primary during the first 72-hour window; please add him to your on-call rotation as the contact for initial troubleshooting.
- Please confirm whether Aurora will provide static NAT egress IPs or require DNS-only allowlisting. Static NAT is strongly preferred for deterministic allowlisting.
- We'll publish a formal IP rotation calendar; for this engagement we'll freeze rotation during your staging window (Dec 8–Dec 12).

If those three items are green, we consider the operator playbook ready for the acceptance run. I'll send the invite for Tue 11/30 10:00 PT and include a short agenda: 1) IP mapping review, 2) verification run, 3) escalation contacts & evidence upload.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
